# Corpus index

The front door for Churchix. How this corpus works and the retrieval budget:
[CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md). How work routes: [routing.md](routing.md). Chronological
changes: [log.md](log.md). The working brief for the code:
[../CLAUDE.md](../CLAUDE.md).

New here? Read [wiki/overview.md](wiki/overview.md), then
[wiki/status.md](wiki/status.md).

## Wiki

<!-- CATALOG:START — generated by lint.sh --index; do not hand-edit -->
- [architecture](wiki/architecture.md) — How Churchix is built. npm-workspaces monorepo, Astro static-first with React islands, shared Zod content schemas, token-only branding, one static build per church. Read before changing package boundaries or the build.
- [content-model](wiki/content-model.md) — The page inventory a church site needs and where its Content Collections and Zod schemas live (packages/schemas). Read before adding a page type or a content field.
- [conventions](wiki/conventions.md) — The cross-cutting rules every churchix brief honors (white-label, tokens-only styling, i18n and diacritics, money, PCI SAQ A, accessibility), the design sources they point at, and the definition of done. Read before building any brief.
- [decisions](wiki/decisions.md) — Settled product and architecture decisions (independent deployments, Orthodox first, static-per-build, Churchix never holds funds) and the owner questions still open (Q4, Q6 to Q10).
- [design-system](wiki/design-system.md) — The Ecclesia Digitalis design system. Tailwind v4 with Material-3 tokens, the seed-versus-derived token contract, and how a church re-skins by tokens alone. Covers the 2026-06-18 liturgical-rail redesign (Rail, PageShell, asymmetric hero) and the max-w guard.
- [donations](wiki/donations.md) — The server-light v1 giving stack (IBAN, Form 230, SMS, pomelnice, hosted card link) and the Romania-specific giving rules. Read before touching giving UI or money handling.
- [i18n-and-glossary](wiki/i18n-and-glossary.md) — Mandatory languages, Romanian diacritic rules, and the domain vocabulary (pomelnice, zeciuială, Form 230 and the rest). Read before writing user-facing strings.
- [independence-model](wiki/independence-model.md) — Why each church is a fully independent deployment with nothing shared at runtime, and why that rules out multi-tenancy. Read before proposing any shared state.
- [optional-backend](wiki/optional-backend.md) — The optional single-tenant Fastify donations API a church can add later for live totals, recurring giving and webhooks, with its data model. Never a shared service and not needed for v1.
- [overview](wiki/overview.md) — What Churchix is. White-label church websites plus giving for Romanian parishes, v1 Orthodox, every church its own static deployment. The orientation page.
- [research-brief-giving](wiki/research-brief-giving.md) — Archive, part two of the original research brief, kept verbatim. The Fastify donations API and payment-provider pick (§4), the giving feature set and PostgreSQL data model (§5), and the ten owner questions (§6). Read §4 and §5 as the optional single-tenant backend, with tenant_id dropped.
- [research-brief](wiki/research-brief.md) — Archive, part one of the original research brief, kept verbatim. The Romanian church-site landscape (§1), the multi-tenancy recommendation later rejected (§2), and the Astro monorepo and content architecture (§3). Read it for the why behind architecture.md.
- [status](wiki/status.md) — Dated snapshot of churchix. What is built, the state and dependencies of all 17 design-integration briefs in one line each, and what is still open. Start here after a break.
- [traditions](wiki/traditions.md) — The two Romanian church markets, Orthodox and evangelical, where they converge and diverge, and what each needs. v1 targets Orthodox.
<!-- CATALOG:END -->

## Work

- [todos/](todos/): captured ideas, pre-spec
- [briefs/todo/](briefs/todo/): numbered work specs, ready to build
- [briefs/done/](briefs/done/) · [briefs/superseded/](briefs/superseded/): the immutable archive

Brief state lives in one line each in [wiki/status.md](wiki/status.md). Don't
read the brief directories wholesale.

## Health

`bash corpus/lint.sh` checks frontmatter, link resolution, page size, abandoned
paths and brief placement. `bash corpus/lint.sh --index` regenerates the catalog
above.
